Tail latency. This is about the time it takes for a request to reach the end of the pipeline. If the system has multiple workers, the tail latency could be the time it takes for the last worker to process the request after the previous one. With disaggregated workers, maybe there's more flexibility in how the tail latency is handled, allowing for better scheduling or load balancing.

Request migration. When a request is processed, if the system has multiple workers, some might switch to handle different tasks. The migration needs to be efficient to minimize disruption. How does the system handle this in a reinforcement learning context? Maybe using a policy to decide when to move requests, or some form of reinforcement learning to optimize the migration.

With disaggregated workers, maybe each worker has a dedicated GPU, so GPU utilization is higher but more predictable. Alternatively, if workers share GPUs, utilization might be lower, but the tradeoff could be more complex.

Throughput tradeoffs. Throughput is the number of requests processed per unit time. With disaggregated workers, the system can distribute tasks across multiple workers, increasing throughput.
